takeaways: Pros and cons of living in Minneapolis, as Jason sees them. Parks lead the pros: the city ranked third in the 2025 ParkScore index, and the Park Board manages more than 185 park properties covering about 7,059 acres.

The Chain of Lakes (Bde Maka Ska, Lake Harriet, Lake of the Isles and Cedar Lake) connects by trail, and the Grand Rounds Scenic Byway loops the city with about 51 miles each of walking and biking paths. Minneapolis is a gold-level Bicycle Friendly Community with about 36 miles of curb-protected bikeways.
Value: the median home price was about $350,000 (up 8.1% from a year earlier) at the time of the video, far below Chicago, Denver or Seattle, and Midwest prices tend to swing less.
Health care and culture: Mayo Clinic is just over an hour away in Rochester, and the city has the Guthrie Theater, First Avenue, Prince's legacy and a James Beard–recognized food scene.

Cons: short summers (the cold season runs roughly November to mid-March), rising prices in popular areas (Linden Hills around $698,000 and Edina around $760,000), year-round road construction and a top state income tax rate of 9.85%.
Winters: the Twin Cities average about 52 inches of snow a year. The people who thrive here embrace winter activities, from skating on frozen lakes to cross-country skiing and fat-tire biking.

faq.q: What are the pros and cons of living in Minneapolis?
faq.a: Pros include one of the best park systems in the country, year-round trails, lower home prices than most big metros, world-class health care nearby and a strong arts and food scene. Cons include long winters, short summers, constant road construction, high state income taxes and rising prices in popular neighborhoods.

faq.q: How much snow does Minneapolis get?
faq.a: About 52 inches a year on average, according to the video.

takeaways: A tour of a new lakefront home on Spring Lake in Prior Lake, built after the original house was torn down, listed at $2,250,000 and shown on the Fall Parade of Homes.
Five bedrooms, four baths and a three-car garage, with 10-foot ceilings, white oak floors, black Andersen windows and a wall of windows facing west over the lake.
The kitchen has a large island, a Wolf range with grill and griddle, a pot filler, a butler's pantry and a walk-in pantry; there's a mudroom off the garage.
Upstairs are four bedrooms, a loft with lake views, laundry next to the owner's suite and an owner's bath with a large tiled shower and soaking tub area.
The home is slab-on-grade because of the lake's high water table. Outside are two maintenance-free decks and about a 75-foot sand beach on Spring Lake, a full recreational lake of about 600 acres.

faq.q: How big is Spring Lake in Prior Lake?
faq.a: About 600 acres, a full recreational lake with good fishing, according to the video.

faq.q: Why don't some lake homes have basements?
faq.a: Where the water table is high near the lake, builders often use a slab-on-grade foundation instead of a basement, as with this Spring Lake home.

takeaways: Jason compares Minnesota's four major cities: Minneapolis, Saint Paul, Rochester and Duluth. The Twin Cities metro has about 3.7 million people.

Population since 2020, as cited: Minneapolis (about 430,000) added only about 400 people, Saint Paul (about 306,000) lost about 4,700, Rochester (about 124,000) grew about 2.4%, and Duluth (about 88,000) grew about 1.7%.

Home prices: Minneapolis in the mid to high $300,000s with the deepest luxury market, Saint Paul around $300,000, Rochester in the mid to high $300,000s, and Duluth around $300,000 with the lowest everyday costs.

Jobs: the Twin Cities have the widest mix, with most of Minnesota's 18 Fortune 500 companies. Rochester runs on health care, with Mayo Clinic's roughly $5 billion downtown expansion expected to add close to 6,000 jobs by about 2030. Duluth leans on tourism, shipping, manufacturing and mining, which rises and falls in cycles.

Commuting: only the Twin Cities have real traffic, and even that is mild by national standards. But MSP Airport, about 10 miles from both downtowns, gives far more flight options than Rochester's or Duluth's regional airports.

Outdoors: Duluth is the gateway to the North Shore of Lake Superior, Rochester is near bluff country and the Root River Trail, and Minneapolis has close to 180 parks and the Grand Rounds inside the city.
Jason's tip: if you're looking at Minneapolis, don't skip Saint Paul. It's 10 to 15 minutes from downtown Minneapolis, shares the same job market and starts at a lower price.

faq.q: Which Minnesota city is the best place to live?
faq.a: It depends on your priorities. Minneapolis offers the most jobs, amenities and housing variety; Saint Paul the same job market at a lower price; Rochester stability from health care; and Duluth the best natural setting and lowest costs.

faq.q: Is Saint Paul cheaper than Minneapolis?
faq.a: Generally, yes. In the video, Saint Paul homes ran around $300,000 versus the mid to high $300,000s in Minneapolis, with far fewer sales over $1 million.

takeaways: A 2023 listing tour of an Apple Valley home with more than 7,300 square feet on a wooded, park-like lot.
Highlights: a gourmet kitchen with Viking appliances, an in-ground pool and patio, and an indoor four-season hot tub.
The owner's suite overlooks the pool, with a soaking tub and custom tiled shower. The large lower level has storage, entertaining space, a tuck-under garage and two stairways.
This home has since sold; see current Apple Valley homes and prices in the market report.

faq.q: Are there homes with pools in Apple Valley?
faq.a: Yes, though in-ground pools are less common in Minnesota. This 2023 tour shows an Apple Valley home with an in-ground pool and an indoor hot tub.

takeaways: A 2022 overview of Burnsville, just south of the Minnesota River, about 20 to 30 minutes from downtown Minneapolis. Neighbors include Bloomington, Eagan, Savage and Apple Valley.
About 64,000 residents and about 68% homeownership. The median home value was in the high $300,000s at the time; see the market report for current prices.

Burnsville has 76 parks and about 300 bodies of water. Crystal Lake, the largest, has a public beach, boat launch and fishing piers, and Buck Hill has the biggest vertical drop of any ski hill in the Twin Cities. Lindsey Vonn got her start there.
Restaurants mentioned include Jensen's Cafe, Porter Creek Hardwood Grill and Buffalo Tap.
Getting around: I-35W, I-35E and Cedar Avenue are close by, MVTA buses serve the area, and the Metro Orange Line runs from Burnsville to downtown Minneapolis.

faq.q: How far is Burnsville from Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 20 to 30 minutes to downtown Minneapolis, and the Metro Orange Line bus rapid transit connects Burnsville to downtown.
In Burnsville, across from Crystal Lake. It has the biggest vertical drop of any Twin Cities ski hill, and Olympic skier Lindsey Vonn got her start there.

takeaways: The Twin Cities' old money came from flour mills, lumber and the railroads of the late 1800s, and it tends to be quiet: historic homes kept and restored rather than torn down. George Dayton's foundation, and the family company's later pledge of 5% of taxable income to charity, shaped that culture.
Kenwood in Minneapolis, planned in 1887, has restored homes mostly built before 1940, a median around $1.1 million to $1.3 million, and vintage homes up to about $5 million.
Lowry Hill was the grand-mansion district (median around $950,000), and Lake of the Isles, East Isles and Cedar-Isles-Dean keep their early-1900s character close to downtown.
Edina's Country Club District, begun in the 1920s, has about 550 homes built from 1924 to 1931 and is on the National Register of Historic Places.

Lake Minnetonka: about 125 miles of shoreline across 37 named bays. Wayzata's median was about $1.8 million (October 2025), Deephaven's median value just over $1 million, and strict shoreline zoning helps protect value.

Saint Paul: Summit Avenue keeps 373 of its original 440 homes along 4.5 miles, including the James J. Hill House (1891), now a National Historic Landmark open for tours. Crocus Hill homes are estimated at about $1.6 million to $1.8 million.
North Oaks, built on James J. Hill's former 3,300-acre farm, has privately owned roads, private wells and septic systems, and trails and conservation areas for residents.

faq.q: Where do wealthy families live in the Twin Cities?
faq.a: Historically in Kenwood, Lowry Hill and around Lake of the Isles in Minneapolis; Summit Avenue and Crocus Hill in Saint Paul; Edina's Country Club District; Lake Minnetonka towns like Wayzata, Deephaven and Orono; and North Oaks.

faq.q: Are the roads in North Oaks private?
faq.a: Yes. North Oaks' roads are owned by the residents, not the city, and every home has a private well and septic system, according to the video.

faq.q: How many original homes are still on Summit Avenue?
faq.a: About 373 of the original 440, along 4.5 miles. It's the longest preserved stretch of Victorian-era homes in the country.
